key_insight: CamPilot improves camera controllability of video diffusion models by introducing an efficient camera-focused reward feedback loop that evaluates alignment in latent space, avoiding costly RGB decoding while enabling stronger camera-conditioned generation.
problem_solved: Existing reward-feedback methods struggle because off-the-shelf reward models cannot reliably assess video–camera alignment and computing rewards by decoding latents to RGB is computationally expensive, limiting practical camera control in video diffusion.
method: Train a lightweight camera-alignment reward model that operates (or is approximated) in the diffusion latent space so alignment can be scored without full RGB decoding.
Integrate the latent-space reward into a reward-feedback fine-tuning loop (CamPilot) to steer the video diffusion model toward trajectories and viewpoints that match camera-control prompts.
Use synthetic/annotated camera trajectories and contrastive/regression-style losses or preference-weighted updates to supervise the reward model and to update the generator efficiently.
impact: This approach enables more precise and computationally efficient camera-conditioned video synthesis, making camera-aware video generation practical for downstream applications like cinematic editing, robotics simulation, and AR/VR content creation.

paper_title: CamPilot: Improving Camera Control in Video Diffusion Model with Efficient Camera Reward Feedback
